questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
questions.explanation: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.

questions.q: Which statement about the Rajya Sabha is correct?
options: It is dissolved every five years.
It is a permanent House, with one-third of its members retiring every two years.
All its members are directly elected.
It can be dissolved by the President.
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is not subject to dissolution; approximately one-third of its members retire every two years.

questions.q: A Money Bill can be introduced in:
options: A joint sitting of both Houses
questions.explanation: A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, on the President's recommendation.

questions.q: The Finance Commission is constituted under which Article?
questions.explanation: Article 280 provides for the constitution of a Finance Commission by the President.

questions.q: Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by which amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 added Fundamental Duties.

questions.q: Who appoints the Governor of a State?
options: The Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.explanation: The President appoints the Governor of each State under Article 155.

questions.q: The President's power to promulgate an Ordinance is available when:
options: Both Houses of Parliament are in session.
At least one House of Parliament is not in session.
The Supreme Court is not in session.
A State declares a financial emergency.
questions.explanation: Under Article 123, the President may promulgate an Ordinance when either House, or both Houses, are not in session and immediate action is necessary.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the Directive Principles of State Policy?
options: They are enforceable by courts in the same way as Fundamental Rights.
They are non-justiciable principles that guide the State.
They apply only during a national emergency.
They can be amended only by State Legislatures.
questions.explanation: Directive Principles are non-justiciable, but are fundamental in the governance of the country.

questions.q: The superintendence, direction and control of elections in India is vested in the:
questions.explanation: Article 324 vests this responsibility in the Election Commission of India.

questions.q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment is primarily associated with:
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions.

questions.q: Which Harappan site is especially noted for its reservoirs and water-management system?
questions.explanation: Dholavira, in present-day Gujarat, is well known for its elaborate reservoirs and water-management structures.

questions.q: The Kalinga War is associated with which Mauryan ruler?
questions.explanation: Ashoka's conquest of Kalinga is described in his Major Rock Edict XIII.

questions.q: The Prayaga Prashasti, an important source for the reign of Samudragupta, was composed by:
questions.explanation: Harishena, a court poet and official, composed the Prayaga Prashasti.

questions.q: The Revolt of 1857 began among sepoys at:
questions.explanation: The sepoy uprising began at Meerut on 10 May 1857 and then spread to other centres.

questions.q: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 with the initiative of:
questions.explanation: A. O. Hume helped organise the first session of the Indian National Congress in 1885.

questions.q: The Swadeshi Movement gathered momentum after which event?
questions.explanation: The 1905 partition of Bengal prompted the Swadeshi and boycott movements.

questions.q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in:
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was adopted by the Congress in 1920.

questions.q: The Dandi March of 1930 was undertaken to protest against the:
questions.explanation: Gandhi's march to Dandi challenged the British salt laws and began the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.q: The Quit India Movement was launched in:
questions.explanation: The Congress launched the Quit India Movement in August 1942.

questions.q: Who was the most prominent leader associated with reorganising and leading the Indian National Army during the Second World War?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose led the Indian National Army and the Provisional Government of Azad Hind.

questions.q: Which river flows westward through a rift valley and empties into the Arabian Sea?
questions.explanation: The Narmada flows west through a rift valley to the Arabian Sea.

questions.q: Black soil is particularly suitable for the cultivation of:
questions.explanation: The moisture-retentive black soils of the Deccan are especially suitable for cotton.

questions.q: The southwest monsoon generally reaches the Indian mainland first along the:
questions.explanation: The Arabian Sea branch of the southwest monsoon normally makes its first landfall over Kerala.

questions.q: Chilika Lake is best described as a:
questions.explanation: Chilika is a brackish-water coastal lagoon on the Odisha coast.

questions.q: The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are located in the:
questions.explanation: The Andaman and Nicobar archipelago lies in the Bay of Bengal.

questions.q: The rain-shadow region of the Deccan Plateau lies mainly to the east of the:
questions.explanation: The Western Ghats intercept moisture-laden winds, leaving areas to their east comparatively dry.

questions.q: The Sundarbans are especially known for which ecosystem?
questions.explanation: The Sundarbans contain one of the world's largest mangrove forest regions.

questions.q: Lakshadweep's islands are primarily of which type?
questions.explanation: Most Lakshadweep islands are coral atolls and reefs.

questions.q: The Standard Meridian of India is approximately:
questions.explanation: Indian Standard Time is based on 82°30′ east longitude.

questions.q: Which gas is a major contributor to the human-caused enhancement of the greenhouse effect?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide released by activities such as fossil-fuel combustion is a major anthropogenic greenhouse gas.

questions.q: Which pigment in green plants absorbs light energy for photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll absorbs light energy used in photosynthesis.

questions.q: The primary role of haemoglobin in red blood cells is to:
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin binds and transports most of the oxygen carried by blood.

questions.q: The SI unit of force is the:
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons, equivalent to kilogram metre per second squared.

questions.q: Why can sound not travel through a vacuum?
options: Sound has no frequency in space.
Sound requires a material medium to transmit vibrations.
Vacuum absorbs all wavelengths of sound.
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs particles in a medium to carry its vibrations.

questions.q: At about 25°C, a neutral aqueous solution has a pH close to:
questions.explanation: At about 25°C, a neutral aqueous solution has pH 7.

questions.q: The human body can synthesise vitamin D in the skin when exposed to:
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet B radiation enables the skin to produce vitamin D3 from a precursor molecule.

questions.q: The ozone layer in the stratosphere is important because it absorbs much of the Sun's:
questions.explanation: Stratospheric ozone absorbs much of the harmful ultraviolet radiation reaching Earth.

questions.q: Acid rain is mainly associated with atmospheric emissions of:
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides can form acids in the atmosphere and contribute to acid deposition.

questions.q: Which action most directly supports in-situ conservation of a threatened wild species?
options: Protecting its natural habitat in a national park
Keeping all individuals in a laboratory
Storing only its DNA in a database
Moving every individual to a zoo
questions.explanation: In-situ conservation protects species within their natural habitats, for example in national parks and sanctuaries.

questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is replenished naturally and is classified as a renewable energy source.

questions.q: Which force is primarily responsible for guarding India's land borders with Pakistan and Bangladesh during peacetime?
questions.explanation: The Border Security Force is primarily tasked with guarding India's borders with Pakistan and Bangladesh.

questions.q: Which force is primarily deployed to guard India's border with China in high-altitude regions?
questions.explanation: The Indo-Tibetan Border Police is deployed along the India-China border, including high-altitude areas.

questions.q: Which organisation is India's central counter-terrorism law-enforcement agency for investigating specified offences?
questions.explanation: The National Investigation Agency investigates offences specified under its governing law, including certain terrorism-related cases.

questions.q: The National Disaster Response Force is primarily organised for:
questions.explanation: The NDRF provides specialist response for natural and human-made disasters.

questions.q: The Central Industrial Security Force is especially associated with security for:
questions.explanation: CISF provides security to critical infrastructure, public-sector units, airports and other designated facilities.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, __.
questions.explanation: The differences are 4, 6, 8 and 10; the next difference is 12, giving 42.

questions.q: A can complete a task in 12 days at a constant rate. What fraction of the task can A complete in 4 days?
questions.explanation: A completes 1/12 of the task per day, so in 4 days A completes 4/12 = 1/3.

questions.q: A vehicle travels 150 kilometres in 3 hours at a constant speed. What is its speed?
questions.explanation: Speed equals distance divided by time: 150 ÷ 3 = 50 km/h.

questions.q: A person walks 4 km north, then 3 km east, then 4 km south. Where is the person relative to the starting point?
questions.explanation: The northward and southward movements cancel, leaving the person 3 km east of the start.

questions.q: If every patrol vehicle is inspected before deployment, and Vehicle P was not inspected, what follows?
options: Vehicle P was not deployed under this rule.
questions.explanation: The rule makes inspection a prerequisite for deployment. If P was not inspected, it was not deployed under that rule.
